queue_items.item: 1. tmpfiles.d byte-identity (df2-10 baked literal vs df1-11 box-resolved birth-write + byte-identical no-op claim)
queue_items.action_taken: Kept DF2.10's ADR-literal `d /run/steering 0700 exedev exedev` as the single canonical byte sequence and edited the DF1.11 side only. AC2(c) now names the canonical bytes explicitly (name form, single-space separated, one trailing newline, nothing else), states the birth-write's $(id -un)/$(id -gn) resolution must reproduce them exactly, and gains the missing negative control: a box whose primary group is not exedev (e.g. `users`) resolves `d /run/steering 0700 exedev users` and MUST fail the driver test loudly on the byte mismatch rather than silently overwrite the image's copy or pass a 'directory exists at 0700' check. AC2(a)'s existing sentence pinning the resolved bytes to DF2.10's literal was already correct and was left alone. No invariant weakened: the byte-identical no-op claim survives and is now falsifiable.

queue_items.item: 2. provisionSteeringChannel post-image role (df2-10 'redundant-but-idempotent, DF1.11 retires it' vs df1-11 'image-regression tripwire at zero diff')
queue_items.action_taken: Edited the DF2.10 side — it was the one that read as retirement. Technical Notes now say: leave the call in place, DF1.11 keeps it as an image-regression tripwire at zero diff whose verify-after-provision assertions fail loudly on a box whose baked entry did not fire, and neither story retires it. Added a matching half-clause to DF1.11 AC2(c) ('the call also stays in place after the image ships, as the image-regression tripwire DF2.10's Technical Notes name') so the agreement is stated in both directions.

queue_items.item: 3. DF1.10 dependency edges vs R10 §2a yaml draft (story omits DF3.3; draft lists it)
queue_items.action_taken: Omission verified sound and KEPT: R7 established src/fleet/resident.ts needs zero code change (the resident relocates because its caller relocates), so no DF3.3-owned line is edited and the repo's list-the-owner-of-the-file-you-modify convention does not trigger. DF3.3 is `done`, so the edge would carry no scheduling information either. The story line is unchanged; the yaml line was corrected instead — deps [DF1.1, DF1.4, DF1.6, DF2.5, DF2.10, DF3.1] with DF3.3 dropped and the reason stated inline in the note (see final_yaml_lines). Story and yaml now agree.

queue_items.item: 4. DF3.7's note: DF1.10 must own the tier3-remote-phases.live.test.ts:154 marker-assertion flip
queue_items.action_taken: Was MISSING from df1-10's Files to Modify (AC7 named the file as a retired stopgap but the file list did not). Added as an 11th entry, scoped to the marker assertion only, with the causal chain stated (`<recordsDir>/<runId>/journal/final.json` at :154 holds only because the retired shim set QDS_RUN_ROOT in its own process, so retiring it flips the assertion onto runMarkerPath()'s in-box path) and DF3.7's disclaimer echoed. Count note: df1-10 Files to Modify goes 10 -> 11, matching the DF3.4 precedent that shipped at 11; no story now claims the file twice.

queue_items.item: 5. pi catalog staged by DF1.10 inside DF2.10's image, unnamed in df2-10
queue_items.action_taken: Added the grant to DF2.10 in the two places an implementer reads it: the Region-ownership note ('DF1.10 adds only the engine build stage — which is also where the pi catalog directory QDS_PI_CATALOG_DIR names is staged, since this story installs pi as a compiled ELF and stages no catalog: that surface is DF1.10-owned inside this image') and the Trigger Surface out-of-scope row (now 'the engine binary, its build stage in this Dockerfile, and the pi catalog directory staged beside it ... DF1.10 owns engine packaging, delivery and the catalog surface (single owner)'). Zero new lines; DF1.10's AC3 and Infra Prerequisite rows already claimed the surface and were left unchanged.

queue_items.item: 6. EnvironmentFile %h vs the literal DF2.10 ships in a system unit
queue_items.action_taken: DF1.10 corrected to DF2.10's literal in all four places (AC3, Infra Prerequisites, Technical Notes, DoD): `EnvironmentFile=/home/exedev/app/.env`. The Technical Notes occurrence carries the one-time reason so the correction cannot be undone by a later reader — '(the literal DF2.10 AC6 bakes — %h in a *system* unit is the manager's home /root, not User=exedev'"'"'s)'. `%h` now appears in the arc exactly twice, both times as the refused form being explained (df2-10:92, df1-10:128). DF1.10's INV-IBOX-4 reference to '$HOME/app/.env' is prose about the delivered key path and stays correct under User=exedev.

queue_items.item: 7. Digest re-pin: df1-10 said it boots 'DF2.10's pinned image' while its own build stage changes the digest
queue_items.action_taken: Aligned DF1.10 to the re-pin in all three places that asserted the identical artifact: E2E slice ('booted from the re-pinned rebuild carrying this story's engine stage — the stage changes the digest, so the pin is re-issued through DF2.10's own pin ritual rather than DF2.10's exact artifact'), AC2(a) ('its build stage changes the digest, so the box boots a re-pinned rebuild inheriting DF2.10's pin ritual — the publish workflow records the digest<->buildId pair; gate B still asserts it'), and the mandatory e2e DoD box. DF2.10's DoD already stated the same thing from its side and needed no edit; the two now match.

queue_items.item: 8. Unset-env guarantees (DF1.11 INV-IBOX-13 QDS_STEERING_ROOT, DF3.7 AC4 QDS_RUN_ROOT) are properties of DF2.10's unit
queue_items.action_taken: DF2.10 was half-done: AC6 carried the obligation normatively but no DoD box made it runnable. Appended it to the Impl DoD box that already runs `systemd-analyze verify` / `systemd-tmpfiles --dry-run` at build — the same check now asserts the rendered unit and the image environment set no QDS_RUN_ROOT, QDS_STEERING_ROOT or any other QDS_* path variable, naming both dependents. Both siblings now cite rather than assume: DF1.11's INV-IBOX-13 gains 'the unit half is DF2.10 AC6's own testable clause and is cited here, not assumed, since only the story that ships the unit can guarantee it', and DF3.7's AC4 gains '(DF2.10 AC6 ships an image and unit that set no QDS_* path variable; cited, not assumed)'. DF3.7's host-leg refusal arm is untouched — it still enforces unset in the reading process rather than trusting the box.

queue_items.item: 9. DF3.7 LOW cleanups (Overview 'run record's approval namespace'; missing Trigger Surface row for the live test)
queue_items.action_taken: Overview now names the normative surface, `run-record.ts`'s approval-extension block, matching AC1, INV-IBOX-14 and the Security DoD box. Added the missing Trigger Surface row: 'the real-box completion -> pause chain, marker written by DF1.10's engine and never planted (AC6) | in-scope | tests/fleet/e2e/tier3-run-completion.live.test.ts | —'. That is the arc's only net-new line (+1); df3-7 goes 134 -> 135 total, well inside its cap.

queue_items.item: 10. DF2.10 scope vs R10 yaml draft (--setup-script threaded in the draft, deliberately not in the story)
queue_items.action_taken: Story is right and unchanged. The yaml line was corrected to two flags with the reason carried inline ('--image/--registry-auth — TWO flags, not three: --setup-script is deliberately NOT threaded because systemd is the boot hook, so its 10 KiB cap is irrelevant'), and while correcting it I also fixed two further draft/story mismatches in the same line: the draft's unqualified 'pin BY DIGEST' now carries AC1(a)/(b)'s honest fallback (immutable tag with the digest recorded in-repo, digest acceptance unverified today), and the unit/tmpfiles/no-QDS_* obligations DF2.10 now owns are stated. See final_yaml_lines.

sweep_findings: INV-IBOX-1..16: each defined exactly once, in its assigned owner, with no gap and no collision (df2-10 1-3, df1-10 4-9, df1-11 10-13, df3-7 14-16). Verified mechanically over the bolded definition form.

Every foreign invariant citation is attributed to its owner: df2-10 -> 'DF1.11's INV-IBOX-13' and 'DF3.7's AC4' (twice each, AC6 and the new DoD clause); df3-7 -> 'DF1.11's INV-IBOX-13' (AC4 and Technical Notes); plus the cross-namespace cites (DF2.3 INV-CRED-1/2/3, DF3.3 INV-RES-1/3/4, DF3.4 INV-APPROVE-5/6, DF2.2 INV-5, DF2.9 INV-5, DF3.6 INV-BND) all carry owner prefixes in the df3-4:257 form.

Sprint headers: all four open identically with '**Sprint:** v5-S3 (in-box restoration arc, story N of 4' and carry the correct ordinal. The tails differ in separator (df2-10/df1-10 use ';', df1-11/df3-7 use an em dash) and in editorial colour. Left as-is: the uniform part is the machine-readable prefix, and forcing the tails identical would delete per-story information for no reader benefit.

Disambiguation line ('pre-2026-08-31 references to DF1.10 owns the round trip ... mean DF1.11 under the ADR's re-charter') is present and substantively identical in the three stories R10 §1 asked for it in: df1-10 (Spec Reference, as 'Renumbering, stated once'), df1-11 and df3-7 (both as a bolded '**Disambiguation:**' bullet). df2-10 correctly omits it — it names neither story's round trip.

File-ownership collisions: four files are touched by more than one story and every one is disjoint by region and attributed on both sides. oci/exedev/Dockerfile (df2-10 authors; df1-10 adds only the engine stage + catalog). src/providers/exedev/driver.ts (df2-10 the two argv spreads + gate B + provenance; df1-11 one && clause inside the existing STEERING_PROVISION_SCRIPT literal + a docblock line — both attribute the file to DF2.2). scripts/fleet.ts (df1-10 registers the run verb; df1-11 the no-ack remediation string only; df3-7 the dispatch block's observer wiring — and df1-10 explicitly disclaims the remediation string as DF1.11's). scripts/pipeline-run.ts (df1-10 run-root resolution + engine-log redirect + marker-exists refusal; df1-11 docstring + sidecar warn + boot-id row).

tier3-remote-phases.live.test.ts is now claimed by exactly one story (df1-10) and explicitly disclaimed by the other (df3-7 region-ownership note and Files-to-Modify parenthetical). No test file is claimed twice anywhere in the arc.

DoD e2e boxes name only tests their own story owns: df3-7 names tier3-run-completion.live.test.ts (its own, new); df1-11's box describes its tier1 inversion without naming a sibling's file; df1-10 and df2-10 describe the run rather than naming a filename. df1-10's forward references ('DF1.11 drains its inbox inside exactly this engine, and DF3.7 polls exactly this marker path') are contract statements, not test claims, and both siblings agree with them.

Shared vocabulary is consistent: PASS-shape language ('no-ack'/exit-6 is the honest shipped shape, 'attach-acked'/exit 0 is the inverted one, a test still passing on no-ack is a false green) appears in the same terms in df1-10 (as the shape it leaves alone) and df1-11 (as the shape it flips); 'claims, not proof' / two-layer evidence doctrine with DF5.1 as the unchanged second layer appears in df1-10 INV-IBOX-7, df1-11's restated INV-RES-4 and df3-7 INV-IBOX-15; the ADR is cited in all four in the R10 §7 form (backticked path, ACCEPTED 2026-08-31, then the Consequence item).

Substrate claims all still trace to the 2026-08-31 probe JSON or are labelled open measurements (df2-10 AC7 a/b/c, AC1a's digest acceptance, df1-10 AC2a's bun:sqlite-in-a-compiled-binary, df1-11's boot ordering). No claim was strengthened past its evidence by any edit above.
Line budgets after all edits: df2-10 201 (unchanged), df1-10 194 (+2), df1-11 142 (unchanged), df3-7 135 (+1). All within the +3 allowance and all inside the atomicity format's normative ceiling.

Residual, recorded not fixed: DF1.10 sits at 8 SP — exactly the atomicity BLOCK ceiling — and this pass confirmed rather than reduced its surface (11 Files to Modify, the engine build stage plus the pi catalog inside DF2.10's Dockerfile, the re-pin through DF2.10's publish workflow, and the tier3 marker-assertion flip). Nothing here is misplaced: each item is the same relocation, and moving any of it to a sibling would split a single owner. But it is the arc's one genuine sizing risk and belongs in the operator's wrap-up note rather than in a story edit.

Residual, benign: DF1.11 declares 'Not an edge — DF2.10' while AC2(c) now pins its birth-write to DF2.10's baked bytes. That remains a correct non-edge — the pin is an assertion the driver test makes, not a build-order requirement, the story stays verifiable on a stock image, and DF2.10 is upstream anyway through DF1.10. No dependency array changes.

Relocates the deterministic TS phase engine AND the resident into the sandbox, restoring §6.2 one-secret-per-box (the host-side resident mints a SECOND capped key, violating INV-RES-3 in substance); records + trace DB written in-box and harvested per §5.3; DF5.1 host re-verify unchanged, preserving R9's two-layer evidence doctrine. NOTE THE RENUMBERING: every pre-2026-08-31 reference to "DF1.10 owns the round trip" (DF3.4 Deviation 12, #180/#181, the fleet attach no-ack remediation string) means DF1.11 now.
final_yaml_lines.DF1.11: DF1.11: { title: "In-Box Steering Executor + Channel Lifecycle", points: 5, status: ready-for-dev, deps: [DF1.10, DF3.3, DF3.4] }  # v5-S3 — in-box restoration arc, story 3 of 4. Closes #181 in its literal on-box reading: the in-box engine consumes /run/steering/inbox.ndjson and writes acks.ndjson ON THE BOX, honouring DF3.4's messageId dedupe; the live e2e PASS shape INVERTS from the honest `no-ack`/exit-6 shipped today to `attach-acked`/exit 0, and a test still passing on no-ack afterwards is a false green. #181's next clause ("engine leg reads/writes through the transport") is SUPERSEDED by the ADR — that transport is the rescinded design; build none. Closes #180 declaratively rather than reactively — the 2026-08-31 probe measured /run as tmpfs, a real reboot wiping /run/steering, and systemd as PID 1, so /etc/tmpfiles.d/qds-steering.conf recreates the channel at boot with no send-failed-triggered re-provision machinery. #180's "telemetry still counts channel recreations" clause is satisfied by ONE boot_id/uptime row per engine start on a reboot-surviving surface (ext4 $HOME engine log or the host driver emit() stream) — NOT by a recreation counter, and it widens neither ResidentTelemetry, the journal resident block, nor DF2.1's closed run record. Birth-writes the same tmpfiles.d drop-in DF2.10 bakes, byte-identical to `d /run/steering 0700 exedev exedev`. MUST update the operator-facing no-ack remediation in scripts/fleet.ts and its four pinned assertions at tests/fleet/gate-verbs.test.ts:1391-1394, all of which name "DF1.10".
final_yaml_lines.DF2.10: DF2.10: { title: "Factory-Owned Boot Image", points: 5, status: ready-for-dev, deps: [DF2.2, DF2.9] }  # v5-S3 — in-box restoration arc, story 1 of 4; strict predecessor of DF1.10. Per ADR 2026-08-31 consequence 1: fork the exeuntu Dockerfile with a pinned bun, a pinned pi and the systemd assets, publish to ghcr.io, and thread --image/--registry-auth through exedev create() — TWO flags, not three: --setup-script is deliberately NOT threaded because systemd is the boot hook, so its 10 KiB cap is irrelevant (the 2026-08-31 probe measured all three available on our plan and the driver passing none, driver.ts:249-255). Pinned BY DIGEST if --image accepts one; digest acceptance is UNVERIFIED today, so AC1's fallback is an immutable tag the workflow refuses to re-push with the digest recorded in-repo, and the Dev Agent Record states which shipped. A baked /etc/qds-image.json buildId is asserted in-box by setup gate B, fail-closed (the box cannot read the digest it was pulled from, and the marker cannot carry a hash of the manifest containing it). Retires the pi 0.55.0/0.84.x drift and makes DF1.6's buildTeamSpawn file:"bun" correct in-box. Ships supervision's image half (ADR consequence 3): a SYSTEM qds-run@.service with Restart=no, User=exedev and the literal EnvironmentFile=/home/exedev/app/.env (%h in a system unit is the manager's home /root), plus /etc/tmpfiles.d/qds-steering.conf as `d /run/steering 0700 exedev exedev` — and it guarantees no QDS_RUN_ROOT, QDS_STEERING_ROOT or other QDS_* path variable is set in image or unit, which is what DF1.11's INV-IBOX-13 and DF3.7's AC4 rest on. DF1.10 later adds the engine build stage and the pi catalog to this Dockerfile and re-pins. Must keep DF2.9's sweep green over the built image's EXPORTED FILESYSTEM (binary image, no npm tree). A registry pull credential is NOT a DF2.3 per-run mint — public image by default, private path handled to DF2.1 assertNoSecret + DF2.2 0600 standards behind a ratified deviation; no dep edge.
final_yaml_lines.DF3.7: DF3.7: { title: "Approval-Gate Bridge", points: 4, status: ready-for-dev, deps: [DF1.10, DF3.4, DF5.1] }  # v5-S3 — in-box restoration arc, story 4 of 4. Per ADR 2026-08-31 consequence 4: the approval gate STAYS HOST-OWNED by construction (its state must outlive the box; approval-gate.ts:8-17 pausing -> teardown -> awaiting-approval is unchanged). CORRECTION OF RECORD, carried as the story's Deviation 1: the phase engine has NEVER called the gate — requestApproval's sole production caller is src/reverify/runner.ts:461, host-side and after the box is torn down — so the ADR's "awaiting marker" wording predates the 2026-08-31 audit and is implemented here as a run-COMPLETION marker, not an approval state; the bridge writes no extensions.approval field and an AC1 static import fence fails the suite if src/fleet/run-completion.ts ever imports approval-gate.ts, approvers.ts, push.ts or run-record.ts. fleet dispatch --await-completion polls the in-box terminal marker through readBoxFile with fan-out's four-kind classification and MARKER_UNUSABLE_TICKS_LIMIT=3, then composes the EXISTING harvest -> teardown -> reverify() chain and re-implements no step. DF5.1 is an edge because it owns the ApprovalPort seam and recordApprovalPort(store) at the reverify call site (runner.ts:430) — the same site DF3.4 round 6 recorded as still owing REAL teardown wiring; DF5.1 already depends on DF3.4, so this adds no cycle. DF2.5 correctly excluded as transitive via DF3.4.
